articles.body:
Secretário Fabio Simões acompanha a instalação das novas estruturas, que vão abrigar mais de 20 leitos — Foto: Secom

A Prefeitura de Rio das Ostras segue com os trabalhos de melhorias e ampliação da infraestrutura de Saúde do Município para melhorar o atendimento à população. Esta semana, começou a instalação das novas estruturas para ampliação do Hospital Municipal, que vai ganhar mais de 20 novos leitos.

Antes da instalação, a Prefeitura já havia preparado a concretagem da base no local que agora recebe os módulos.

“Estamos investindo na ampliação e melhoria da infraestrutura de toda a Rede Municipal de Saúde: postos, Centro de Saúde e também do Hospital Municipal. Estamos trabalhando no resgate da nossa Cidade. Melhorar o atendimento à população e as condições de trabalho dos profissionais de Saúde são nossas prioridades”, disse o prefeito Carlos Augusto Balthazar.

MAIS LEITOS – A nova área vai receber especialmente pacientes do setor de Trauma, do Pronto-Socorro, que estarão mais próximo do Centro de Imagem do Hospital de Setor Cirúrgico.

Além de ampliar a capacidade de internação da Unidade, os novos leitos do Hospital servirão para agilizar o atendimento aos pacientes, incluindo vítimas de acidentes ou outros casos que necessitam de exames como tomografia computadorizada e ultrassom ou procedimentos cirúrgicos.

“Essa expansão vai ser um ganho muito grande para a Saúde no nosso Município porque pacientes da emergência que precisam fazer exames como tomografia, ultrassom ou passar por cirurgia serão atendidos no próprio Hospital sem necessidade de deslocamento por ambulância. Vamos agilizar atendimento, otimizar o uso de recursos e salvar vidas. Estamos mantendo nosso compromisso de oferecer uma Saúde de qualidade e um atendimento humanizado à população”, explica o secretário de Saúde, Fábio Simões.

O secretário informa ainda que essa ampliação era uma prioridade máxima da Gestão Municipal, melhorando tanto a resposta de atendimento ao paciente quanto a logística da emergência, que hoje sobrecarrega o Pronto-Socorro.

“O Hospital conta com os exames de imagem, cirurgia geral, ortopédica, buco-maxilo, entre outros serviços que estão diretamente ligados ao atendimento do Trauma. Esses serviços estão disponíveis 24 horas. Vamos ganhar muito, muito tempo no atendimento e agilizar a logística beneficiando os pacientes e profissionais de saúde”, completa Simões.

articles.title: Pesquisa clínica em câncer: etapas para novos tratamentos | G1
articles.standfirst: Antes de chegar à prática clínica, novos tratamentos passam por etapas de pesquisa, avaliação e acompanhamento.
articles.summary: Antes de chegar à prática clínica, novos tratamentos passam por etapas de pesquisa, avaliação e acompanhamento.
articles.body:
O desenvolvimento de novos medicamentos e estratégias para o tratamento do câncer envolve diferentes etapas antes que essas alternativas possam chegar à prática clínica. Esse processo inclui estudos realizados com participantes humanos para avaliar aspectos como segurança, eficácia e possíveis efeitos adversos.

É nesse contexto que está a pesquisa clínica, área dedicada à produção de evidências sobre medicamentos, tratamentos e outras intervenções. No Hospital Erasto Gaertner, os estudos são conduzidos pelo Centro de Projetos de Ensino e Pesquisa (CEPEP), unidade da Liga Paranaense de Combate ao Câncer criada em 1985.

A instituição iniciou a condução de estudos clínicos após a criação de seu Comitê de Ética em Pesquisa, em 1999. Atualmente, o CEPEP informa manter mais de 100 estudos clínicos em diferentes etapas, desde o processo regulatório até o encerramento.

Pesquisa clínica é o nome dado aos estudos realizados com participantes humanos para avaliar medicamentos, tratamentos ou outras intervenções. Cada pesquisa parte de uma pergunta científica e segue um protocolo que define objetivos, critérios de participação, consultas, exames, tratamento previsto, duração e formas de acompanhamento.

No Hospital Erasto Gaertner, os estudos clínicos passam previamente pelo Comitê de Ética em Pesquisa (CEP) da instituição e seguem as exigências éticas e regulatórias aplicáveis.

O CEPEP mantém um fluxo específico para as diferentes etapas dos estudos, considerando aspectos como rigor científico, integridade dos participantes e qualidade da pesquisa.

Quais são as fases de um estudo clínico?

O desenvolvimento clínico de um medicamento costuma ser organizado em diferentes fases. Cada uma tem objetivos específicos e contribui para ampliar o conhecimento sobre a intervenção estudada.

Na Fase I , um dos principais objetivos é avaliar aspectos relacionados à segurança, aos efeitos adversos, ao comportamento da substância no organismo e às faixas de dose.

Na Fase II , a pesquisa amplia a avaliação sobre a eficácia para determinada doença e continua acompanhando aspectos de segurança.

Já na Fase III , um número maior de participantes é estudado. Nessa etapa, o tratamento em investigação pode ser comparado às alternativas já utilizadas, conforme o protocolo da pesquisa.

A Fase IV ocorre após a aprovação e comercialização do medicamento e permite reunir informações adicionais sobre riscos, benefícios e utilização em condições mais amplas.

O Complexo Erasto Gaertner informa realizar estudos clínicos em todas essas fases.

Quem pode participar de uma pesquisa clínica?

A participação em um estudo clínico depende dos critérios estabelecidos em cada protocolo. Por isso, uma pesquisa disponível no hospital não significa que todos os pacientes possam participar.

Os critérios de elegibilidade podem considerar fatores como diagnóstico, estágio da doença, tratamentos anteriores, condições clínicas, resultados de exames e outras características previstas no estudo.

No Hospital Erasto Gaertner, o paciente interessado deve conversar com o médico responsável. A partir dessa avaliação, a equipe pode verificar se existe algum estudo compatível com o caso e se os critérios definidos no protocolo são atendidos.

Profissionais e estudantes participam de atividade de ensino e pesquisa no Hospital Erasto Gaertner. — Foto: Divulgação/Erasto Gaertner.

Sim. A participação em uma pesquisa clínica depende da decisão voluntária do paciente, após o recebimento das informações sobre o estudo e a possibilidade de esclarecer dúvidas com a equipe responsável.

Essa decisão é registrada por meio do Termo de Consentimento , documento que apresenta informações sobre a pesquisa, os procedimentos previstos, possíveis riscos e benefícios e outros aspectos necessários para que a pessoa possa decidir de forma esclarecida.

A existência de um estudo, portanto, não representa inclusão automática. A participação depende dos critérios definidos no protocolo, da avaliação da equipe e da decisão do paciente.

O participante paga pelo tratamento do estudo?

Segundo as orientações institucionais do Hospital Erasto Gaertner, o participante não tem custo com o tratamento relacionado ao estudo clínico e também não recebe pagamento pela participação.

Em determinadas situações, pode existir ressarcimento de despesas relacionadas à participação, como gastos com transporte para consultas e exames. As condições podem variar conforme cada pesquisa e devem ser esclarecidas diretamente com a equipe responsável pelo estudo.

Como funciona a pesquisa clínica no Erasto Gaertner?

O CEPEP realiza pesquisas patrocinadas, estudos de iniciativa do investigador e pesquisas colaborativas. Atualmente, a instituição informa manter mais de 100 estudos clínicos em diferentes estágios, desde o processo regulatório até o encerramento.

O fluxo institucional envolve etapas como processo regulatório, recrutamento de participantes, desenvolvimento do estudo, acompanhamento previsto pelo protocolo e encerramento.

As pesquisas abrangem diferentes áreas da oncologia. O portal do CEPEP disponibiliza estudos organizados por categorias como cabeça e pescoço, cardiologia oncológica, hematologia, mama, pediatria, pele e pulmão, além de pesquisas que envolvem múltiplas áreas.

Por que a pesquisa clínica é importante para a oncologia?

O desenvolvimento dos tratamentos contra o câncer depende da produção contínua de evidências científicas. Por meio da pesquisa clínica, diferentes hipóteses podem ser avaliadas, tratamentos podem ser comparados e novos medicamentos e estratégias terapêuticas podem avançar nas etapas de desenvolvimento.

Para uma instituição oncológica, a estrutura de pesquisa também aproxima assistência, ciência e formação profissional. No CEPEP, médicos, profissionais de enfermagem e de outras áreas, acadêmicos, residentes e pesquisadores participam de atividades científicas em diferentes frentes.

Para o paciente, a existência de estudos clínicos pode representar uma possibilidade a ser avaliada junto ao médico, caso exista um protocolo compatível com sua condição.

Essa possibilidade, porém, depende dos critérios de cada pesquisa e da avaliação individual. A participação em um estudo não representa garantia de benefício terapêutico.

Como saber quais pesquisas estão recrutando pacientes?

O CEPEP mantém em seu portal uma área dedicada à pesquisa clínica, com informações sobre os estudos e as categorias de pesquisas disponíveis.

O paciente interessado deve conversar com seu médico para verificar se existe algum protocolo compatível com seu diagnóstico e suas condições clínicas.

A equipe de pesquisa do Hospital Erasto Gaertner também disponibiliza canais de contato para orientações sobre participação em estudos clínicos.

O Centro de Projetos de Ensino e Pesquisa (CEPEP) do Hospital Erasto Gaertner foi fundado em 1985 e atua nas áreas de pesquisa clínica e ensino.

A estrutura alcança unidades da Liga Paranaense de Combate ao Câncer, incluindo o complexo hospitalar Erasto Gaertner e o Hospital Erastinho.

O centro conta com equipe especializada e integração com os recursos assistenciais e tecnológicos da instituição, participando de estudos clínicos em diferentes áreas da oncologia.

articles.title: Heart health: Don’t let social media convince you Vitamin D and K2 can ‘clean’ your arteries; this viral health claim comes with a caveat
articles.summary: A vitamin bottle can look like a surprisingly simple answer to a complicated heart problem.
articles.body: A vitamin bottle can look like a surprisingly simple answer to a complicated heart problem. On social media, vitamin D and vitamin K2 are often presented as a powerful pair that can supposedly stop calcium from settling in the arteries and even help “clean” them. The explanation sounds neat: vitamin D helps with calcium absorption, while K2 is said to direct calcium towards the bones instead of the arteries.But there is a problem with that neat little story.Vitamin D and vitamin K do play important roles in calcium metabolism and bone health. And researchers have been studying whether they may also influence vascular calcification. But that does not mean taking D and K2 supplements can clear calcium that has already accumulated in the arteries.“Vitamin K2 and vitamin D have been getting attention for their possible role in managing calcium buildup in the arteries. Many influencers and short-video creators are promoting vitamin K2 and D, saying these two vitamins can ‘clean’ calcium buildup in arteries. They claim that vitamin K2 guides calcium towards the bones and prevents it from building up in the arteries. Vitamin D also helps with calcium absorption. These claims create a perception that using vitamin K2 and D supplements can reduce calcium buildup in arteries. But this is not the true conclusion,” Dr (Col) Anil Dhall, Director & HOD – Cardiology, Sarvodaya Hospital, told TOI Health.What did the DANCODE study actually find?Part of the recent interest comes from the Danish DANCODE trial, which looked at whether vitamin D3 and vitamin K2 supplementation could influence the progression of coronary artery calcification.According to Dr Dhall, the findings showed a slowing in the progression of calcification with the vitamin combination. But that is very different from saying the supplements removed existing calcium.“Intake of both the vitamins slowed down the progression of calcification. However, it did not clear calcium altogether,” he said.And that difference is easy to lose when a scientific finding is turned into a short social-media video.“People may hear that calcium progresses more slowly and assume that the vitamins are cleaning the arteries. That is not what the study showed. It is a finding about the progression of calcification, not proof that existing calcium can be removed,” Dr Dhall said.In other words, slower progression should not be turned into ‘calcium has been cleared’.Why are vitamin K2 and vitamin D being discussed in the first place?There is a real biological reason these vitamins have attracted attention.“Vitamin K is involved in activating proteins that help regulate calcium in the body. This is why K2 is sometimes described as a kind of ‘traffic police’ for calcium. It helps direct calcium towards bones and away from inappropriate deposits,” Dr Dhall said.Vitamin K can be obtained through food, including fermented foods and some dairy products and eggs. But the fact that vitamin K participates in calcium regulation does not automatically mean that taking a K2 supplement will prevent arterial calcification.That is where social-media explanations can get ahead of the evidence.Vitamin D, meanwhile, is essential for calcium absorption and bone health. But more vitamin D is not necessarily better for the heart.“The DANCODE trial used 1,000 IU of vitamin D3 daily. It should not be interpreted as support for taking high-dose vitamin D without medical supervision,” Dr Dhall said.“Vitamin D is important when the body needs it, but more is not always better. High-dose supplementation should have a reason behind it and, when necessary, should be monitored,” he added.A calcium score does not mean you need a vitaminA coronary artery calcium (CAC) score is used to detect calcified plaque in the coronary arteries. A higher score can indicate a greater burden of calcified plaque and may be one part of assessing cardiovascular risk.But seeing a high number on a report should not automatically send someone looking for a bottle of K2.“Taking a K2 supplement simply because a calcium score is high is not something people should decide on their own. Vitamin K can also interfere with some medicines,” Dr Dhall said.This is particularly relevant for people taking medicines such as warfarin, where vitamin K intake can affect anticoagulation.So if a person has been told they have coronary artery calcification, the next step is not necessarily a supplement. The bigger question is why that person has cardiovascular risk and how it should be managed.Vitamins are not “pipe cleaners” for your arteriesThis may be the most important takeaway from the entire vitamin D-K2 conversation.“The most important message is that vitamins are not ‘pipe cleaners’ for blocked arteries. A high calcium score is a reason to take cardiovascular risk seriously, not a reason to start a collection of supplements,” Dr Dhall said.Blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol, tobacco use, physical activity, diet and prescribed medicines can all form part of cardiovascular risk management.The temptation to find one supplement that fixes a complicated health problem is understandable. Social media makes that temptation even stronger because a complicated biological process can be squeezed into a 30-second explanation.But arteries are not pipes, and supplements are not cleaning products.Vitamin D and K2 have genuine biological roles. Researchers are studying whether they can influence vascular calcification. The evidence, however, should not be stretched into a promise that these vitamins can clean out calcium from your arteries.That is the caveat worth remembering before turning a viral health claim into a daily supplement routine.

articles.title: Rescuers search for 12 missing after Nepal avalanche kills two
articles.summary: Rescue teams resume search for missing people after avalanche on Himlung Himal killed two people during severe weather.
articles.body:
Rescuers are searching for a dozen people swept away by an avalanche that killed at least two others on a Nepalese mountain during severe weather.

At least 10 people have been rescued from Mount Himlung, a 7,126-metre (23,380-foot) peak in north-central Nepal after the avalanche hit on Sunday.

The remains of the two people who were killed were airlifted on Monday to Kathmandu airport and transported to the Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.

“Two bodies were found as rescuers worked until 6pm (12:30 GMT) last night,” Tul Singh Gurung, president of the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, told the AFP news agency. “The search continues for 14 expedition workers who are still missing.”

A team of eight mountain guides is involved in the search operation, he added.

All those killed or missing were Nepali nationals. The avalanche hit as they were at a base camp preparing for foreign clients to arrive and climb the peak during the autumn climbing season that began this month.

Flooding and landslides were reported in the Manang district, where the mountain is located, over the weekend, both caused by heavy rainfall, the district administration said.

The avalanche comes as the government issued warnings of severe weather across the entire Himalayan nation.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said 21 other people were killed and five more are missing in different parts of the country between Thursday and Sunday.

Nepal is recovering from devastating flooding in August that swept away several villages, killing more than 1,400 people.

According to NDRRMA, 5,500 people were still missing and 13,795 had been rescued.

Researchers from the World Weather Attribution (WWA) group said in a report released last week that the disaster was not caused by a single extreme weather event but rather a “compound crisis” shaped by long-term warming, glacier retreat, permafrost thaw and geological instability.

articles.title: Popular weight-loss drugs can become an ‘atomic bomb’ at high doses, doctor warns
articles.summary: Dr. Will Cole warns that macro-dosing GLP-1s isn't the answer to metabolic health, advocating for micro-dosing peptides paired with lifestyle changes.
articles.body: As interest in peptides continues to grow, experts are increasingly looking beyond weight loss to their potential role in healthy aging. Functional medicine expert Dr. Will Cole told Fox News Digital that peptides are "intimately connected" with longevity, cellular healing and metabolic health. "[Peptides] help with cellular communication," said Cole, co-author of the upcoming book "Heal Your Cells." The recommendations for peptides depend on the context in which they're used, he said, noting that the answer often falls "somewhere in the middle." THINKING ABOUT PEPTIDES? DOCTORS REVEAL KEY DOS AND DON’TS AS ‘WILD WEST’ MARKET GROWS Citing previous research, Cole noted that an estimated 93% of U.S. adults are metabolically unhealthy, leaving only about 7% who meet the criteria for optimal metabolic health — a figure he described as "wild." "That's common, but not normal," Cole said. He added that while GLP-1 medications can be beneficial, improving metabolic health also requires addressing lifestyle and other underlying factors. FDA TO REVIEW 7 POPULAR PEPTIDES TOUTED FOR WEIGHT LOSS, HEALING AND LONGEVITY Cole shared that he does not believe "macro-dosing" GLP-1s "forever and ever in perpetuity" is the solution to improving metabolic health. While GLP-1s can reduce food cravings — often referred to as "food noise" — and promote weight loss, Cole said he’d like to see more research on how decreasing the desire for food could also decrease cravings for love, relationships and other mood-boosting factors. Cole questioned whether suppressing food cravings could have unintended effects on other reward-related behaviors, including social relationships. "So, are we circumventing pathways and pathologizing things that don't have to be pathologized?" CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Cole argued that some degree of hunger signaling is healthy. "Food noise is actually a decent thing in balance, so shutting down your hunger cues with an 'atomic bomb' peptide dose is not the solution." He added that he believes overreliance on GLP-1 medications may contribute to disordered eating patterns and a growing fear of hunger. Cole attributed the trend to a culture that favors simple, fast solutions over sustained lifestyle changes. "We want a magic pill," he said. "And the truth is somewhere in the middle: Can we micro-dose? Can we do it cyclically? And can we pair it with lifestyle?" CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER The expert questioned why there has been an "epidemic rise" of metabolic problems, pointing to factors such as diets high in ultraprocessed foods, nutrient deficiencies, environmental toxins and the presence of stress and trauma. "That is why we're seeing a rise of chronic health problems, not a pharmaceutical deficiency," he said. Cole said he supports wider access to peptides, but emphasized the importance of transparency, product purity and clear labeling so healthcare professionals and consumers can make informed decisions. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Despite those concerns, Cole said he believes GLP-1s also hold significant therapeutic promise, citing their potential to reduce inflammation, help manage autoimmune conditions and improve gut health. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "But again, what's the lowest dose that yields a beneficial result paired with lifestyle? I think that's where peptides can really shine," he said. "And I am actually more excited about some of these other [peptides], like the inflammation ones or the longevity peptides."

articles.title: Dietitian Shares Her Go-To High-Protein Snack That Boosts Brain Health
articles.summary: This dietitian-approved snack is plant-based and contains nutrients to boost brain health. You’ll also get some filling protein and gut-healthy fiber.
articles.body: Eating for better brain health isn’t hard when it’s delicious. And this dietitian-recommended recipe is both tasty and good for your noggin. The star of the show is walnuts, which are touted for their brain- and heart-heath boosting nutrients. But walnuts are also a source of healthy, filling plant-based protein, and this subtly sweet and crunchy snack will make you want to reach for more. Nutrition Tip of the Day: Try This Plant-Based Snack for an Easy Brain Health Boost This simple, delicious recipe is a winner for brain health, says Natalie Rizzo, registered dietitian and TODAY nutrition editor. Her Cinnamon Roasted Walnuts recipe is a flavorful, sweet-and-salty concoction that takes just 10 minutes in the oven to make. And the walnuts the recipe relies are packed with nutrients that benefit your brain. While they may be reminiscent of candied nuts, these walnuts are tossed with just a hint of maple syrup to keep them from getting too sweet. Why It Matters Walnuts are one of the healthiest nuts you can eat and one of the most beneficial foods for brain health and heart health. They’re rich in a type of plant omega-3 fatty acid called alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), which has been linked to both heart and brain health, TODAY.com explained previously. Walnuts also contain an amino acid called L-arginine which both support your heart. Walnuts also provide a bit of fiber and healthy plant protein, about 4 grams per 1-ounce serving. Of course, walnuts alone aren’t the secret to lasting brain and heart health. But eating walnuts as part of an overall healthy lifestyle may be beneficial, and research has linked regular walnut consumption to better cognitive health and improvements in cholesterol numbers. How to Get Started Rizzo’s recipe is simple. It only requires four ingredients and 10 minutes in the oven. And you can feel free to customize it the way you like it. Use honey instead of maple syrup, for instance, or add other warm, fall spices. While these tasty walnuts make a great, crunchy snack on their own, try pairing them with other brain- and heart-healthy foods to get even more benefits. For instance, eat them with fresh blueberries over Greek yogurt, or use them to top a veggie-packed salad. articles.title: I’m a Physician of 18 Years. Say This 1 Phrase to Your Doctor If You Feel Like Your Concerns Aren’t Being Addressed
articles.summary: With just a few months left in the year, you may find yourself scrambling to get all of your doctors’ appointments taken care of, from your annual physical to skin checks and teeth cleanings.
articles.body: With just a few months left in the year, you may find yourself scrambling to get all of your doctors’ appointments taken care of, from your annual physical to skin checks and teeth cleanings. When you only see your doctor once a year, it can be challenging to make sure the visit addresses all of your health concerns, especially if you only have a few minutes with your provider. That’s why family physician Dr. Jen Caudle says it’s important to tell them upfront if you have more than one issue you’d like to talk through. Expert Tip of the Day: Ask Your Doctor for a ‘Plan’ for Any Issues You Wanted Addressed in Greater Detail “You deserve a plan of action for every concern that you bring up to your doctor,” Caudle says. “That plan of action can range from ... when I see you in two weeks, when we go over your lab work, let’s talk more about that insomnia” to prescribing medication, testing or seeing a specialist, she adds. “It’s OK to, for lack of better word, remind your doctor about what you mentioned prior that you didn’t get to either resolve or a definitive plan about.” Why It Matters While it may feel uncomfortable to try to take control of your own care, many doctors often appreciate the extra attention to detail from their patients. “Sometimes, honestly, we’re just going through our list of stuff and ... we just forget as we’re writing our notes and seeing you in the office right, so I appreciate the reminder, like, ‘Oh hey, what about the refill I need?’” Caudle says. “So sometimes it’s it’s a group effort, and I also want patients to know it is their right, and they deserve a plan for everything.” How to Get Started Caudle says that the best approach for getting your concerns addressed starts even before the appointment. First, make a list of everything you want to talk through, including your symptoms, when they started and other relevant details. Then, let your doctor know at the very beginning of the appointment that you have multiple things you’d like to talk through. That way, they can decide which are the highest priority and which can be dealt with more quickly or at a follow-up appointment. And don’t forget to be honest with your doctor about how an issue is impacting your life — there’s no need to downplay, Caudle says. “Sometimes patients are very considerate of their doctor in ways I don’t need them to be,” she adds. articles.title: Malicious browser extensions can hijack AI assistants
articles.summary: BragJack research reveals how a single malicious browser extension could hijack Gemini, Perplexity Comet and Edge AI agents with zero clicks.
articles.body: AI assistants are moving deeper into the browsers we use every day. They can summarize a webpage, explain what you are looking at and, in some cases, take action on websites for you. That convenience also gives these tools access that a normal webpage would never have. Now, security researcher Gal Weizman of Forever Security has shown how a malicious browser extension could potentially turn those powerful AI capabilities against you. His research, called BragJack, targeted Gemini Live in Chrome, Perplexity Comet, Microsoft Edge Actions, Opera Neon and Anthropic's Claude in Chrome. The findings resulted in more than $20,000 in bug bounties and two CVEs. There is one important detail before you panic. The attack still required the malicious extension to be installed first. After that, Weizman demonstrated attacks that needed zero additional clicks from the victim. So how could one extension get that far inside the browser? It comes down to how these AI assistants are built. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways AI can help you get better healthcare. Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Get Better Healthcare With AI, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed. Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com. AI MALWARE CAN REWRITE ITSELF TO EVADE DETECTION How a malicious extension can reach your browser's AI Weizman describes these AI systems as having a "brain" and a "body." The AI model works out what should happen. A privileged component inside the browser then carries out the request. Depending on the product, that privileged component might read webpage content, capture a screenshot or interact with a website. That setup becomes risky if something else inside the browser can manipulate the connection between those pieces. The proof-of-concept attacks relied heavily on Chromium's declarativeNetRequest, or DNR, system. Browser extensions can use DNR to modify how network requests work. That can include changing response headers or redirecting resources. Forever Security showed how those capabilities could let an extension interfere with web content trusted by a browser's AI features. Chrome's Gemini flaw exposed files and screenshots Chrome was one of the more striking examples. Google's Gemini side panel essentially has two pieces. Gemini handles the intelligence behind the request while Chrome provides the browser-level abilities needed to carry it out. Researchers found that Chrome already prevented extensions from directly injecting scripts into the Gemini page. However, the researchers discovered that an extension could still manipulate certain network requests used inside the Gemini experience. That gap allowed Weizman to demonstrate access to browser capabilities that the extension itself should never have received. According to the research, he could access local files, capture screenshots and obtain browser profile information. The researcher says the flaw also let him turn on the camera and microphone with zero clicks from the user. Google awarded the researchers a $7,000 bounty for reporting the vulnerability, which received the identifier CVE-2026-0628. Google has since confirmed to CyberGuy that it has closed this specific attack path. A Google spokesperson told us, "Confirming we've released a patch in Chrome so this method no longer works on the Gemini side panel." That means the technique demonstrated by the researchers should no longer work against the Gemini side panel in an updated version of Chrome. Perplexity Comet could take the attack further Perplexity Comet raised a different concern because its AI agent can take actions inside websites. Weizman found that Comet's built-in agent trusted several Perplexity domains. One testing domain lacked the same extension protections used on the main Perplexity site. Normally, that testing address redirected elsewhere. The proof-of-concept used DNR to remove the redirect and load the page instead. That gave the extension a path to communicate with Comet's built-in agent. The demonstrated access included browsing history, screenshots and local files. Then things became more personal. Weizman demonstrated sending an instruction that told the agent to access Perplexity, summarize the victim's recent emails and send the information to another email address. The AI agent performed the browser actions using capabilities it already had. Microsoft Edge had safeguards that researchers bypassed Microsoft built safeguards into Edge to keep outside prompts from easily controlling what its AI agent could do. Researchers still found a way around them. Weizman discovered a timing flaw known as a race condition. In simple terms, his test extension could feed the AI a prompt and then quickly switch on its ability to take action before Edge finished checking whether the request should be allowed. That opened the door for the AI agent to carry out a command it should not have accepted. Microsoft tracked the flaw as CVE-2026-55945 and rated it medium severity. The company says Edge versions before 150.0.4078.48 were affected. Updating Edge closes this particular security hole. Opera Neon and Claude in Chrome were vulnerable too Forever Security also demonstrated related attacks against Opera Neon and Claude in Chrome. There is an important difference with Claude. Claude in Chrome is itself a browser extension, rather than a complete browser. The researcher found that a page on Claude's domain could send prompts to the extension's side panel. Another extension could manipulate that trusted page and force prompts into Claude. Forever Security says Anthropic awarded a bounty for the finding and classified it as medium severity. Opera Neon also allowed the proof-of-concept extension to reach its AI agent. According to the researcher, that access could force the agent to carry out instructions on websites. All five demonstrations were Chromium-based, which helped the researcher reuse the same basic attack approach. We reached out to Google, Microsoft, Perplexity, Opera and Anthropic for comment on the research. Google responded with the update included above. Microsoft pointed us to its CVE-2026-55945 security advisory and said it had nothing further to share. We did not hear back from Perplexity, Opera or Anthropic before our deadline. LOCK DOWN YOUR CHATGPT ACCOUNT BEFORE THE NEXT AI ATTACK Prompt Forcing gives attackers another way to abuse AI You may already have heard about prompt injection. That usually involves hiding malicious instructions in something an AI reads. Weizman calls this new approach Prompt Forcing. Here, the attacker does not need to hide instructions inside a webpage and hope the AI follows them. The attacker can force a complete prompt into the agent through a channel that the browser or assistant trusts. The AI can then turn that plain-English instruction into legitimate browser actions. That creates an interesting problem for security software. A suspicious program stealing an email may be easier to spot. An approved AI agent opening a website and clicking a button can look like normal browser activity. The published BragJack research describes proof-of-concept attacks and does not report that these techniques have been exploited in the wild. Still, the research shows how the security equation changes as AI agents receive deeper access to browsers and computers. Why you should take another look at your browser extensions The attack starts with something many of us barely think about anymore: a browser extension. CyberGuy has covered malicious extensions that pretended to be AI assistants, hijacked online accounts and even turned trusted extensions into data-stealing spyware. That makes extension cleanup one of the easiest steps you can take right now. Maybe you installed a coupon extension two years ago and forgot about it. Perhaps you tested an AI sidebar once and never opened it again. If you no longer need an extension, there is little reason to keep giving it access to your browser. 8 ways to protect yourself from malicious browser extensions 1) Keep your browser updated Browsers receive security fixes regularly, so install updates as soon as they become available. Google's response makes that especially relevant here. The company says it has already released the Chrome patch that blocks the Gemini side-panel method demonstrated by the researchers. Restart Chrome after an update if prompted so the newest version can finish installing. 2) Remove extensions you no longer use Open your browser's extension manager and remove anything you do not recognize or no longer use. Here is the quickest way to check: Chrome and Claude in Chrome: Click the three-dot menu → Extensions → Manage extensions → find the extension → Remove. Google confirms this path in its current Chrome instructions. Microsoft Edge: Click the Extensions puzzle-piece icon → Manage extensions → find the extension → Remove. Opera Neon: Open the Extensions area from the browser sidebar or menu → review your installed extensions → remove anything you no longer trust or use. Opera documents its extensions manager through the Extensions icon and menu. Perplexity Comet: Open the browser's extensions manager and review imported or installed Chrome extensions. Comet supports Chrome extensions and can import them from Chrome. Pro tip: If you are unsure about an extension, disable it first and research the developer before removing it. THOUSANDS OF HACKED SITES TRICK YOU INTO INSTALLING MALWARE 3) Check permissions before installing Look carefully when an extension asks for broad access to websites or browser activity. The permission should make sense for what the extension actually does. 4) Limit an extension's access when possible Some browsers let you decide whether an extension can run on every website or only certain sites. Give an extension the narrowest access it needs to work. 5) Be careful with AI extensions An extension that uses a familiar AI name may have no connection to the company behind that AI service. Check the publisher before installing it. 6) Turn off AI browser features you do not use If your browser gives you the option to disable an AI assistant or agent you never use, consider turning it off. That reduces the number of powerful browser features available if another component gets compromised. 7) Use strong antivirus software Strong antivirus software can help flag malicious downloads and suspicious activity connected to bad extensions. It adds another layer of protection if something slips past you. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com. 8) Treat extensions like apps Do not install one because it sounds useful for five minutes. Every extension adds code and permissions to the browser you use for email, banking, shopping and other private activity. Kurt's key takeaways What gets my attention here is how much more powerful a bad browser extension can become when an AI agent enters the picture. We already knew extensions could spy on browsing or steal account data. This research shows a possible path to something with much broader privileges. There is also a practical takeaway. These demonstrations still required the attacker-controlled extension to get inside the browser first. Once it was there, however, the researcher showed that the attack could continue without another click from the victim. I would take five minutes and look through your extensions today. If you cannot remember why you installed one, find out what it does. If you stopped using it months ago, remove it. As browser AI grows more capable, the companies building these tools also need strong barriers between ordinary extensions and the privileged systems that let AI act for us. Would you still let an AI assistant control parts of your browser if a malicious extension could potentially turn that access against you? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com. articles.title: I'm 25 with a terminal disease. We need an FDA commissioner that hears people like me
articles.summary: A 25-year-old living with Duchenne muscular dystrophy explains why the Senate confirmation fight over FDA nominee Dr. Heidi Overton is personal.
articles.body: I just turned 25. People with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) aren't expected to see another birthday after this one. DMD is a progressive disease; my muscles weaken over time and things that used to be automatic now take planning, assistance, or simply aren't possible anymore. Even sleeping can be hard. Bed sores are now an issue. Basic physical function takes work most people never have to think about. I know what the statistics say. I am not ready to let them write the ending of my story. TRUMP FDA PICK REPEATEDLY SIDESTEPS SANDERS' UNIVERSAL HEALTHCARE DEMANDS IN HEATED CLASH I want to grow my career, I want to get married and start a family. I want to wake up decades from now and realize that turning 25 wasn't the beginning of the end — it was just another birthday I was blessed enough to reach. That's why I'm watching the Senate confirmation fight over Dr. Heidi Overton, the nominee to lead the FDA, more closely than most 25-year-olds ever watch Washington. For most Americans, an FDA commissioner is just another name in the news. For the 30 million Americans like me living with a rare disease, that person can decide how many options I have and how much time I have to use them. To be clear: I'm not asking the FDA to abandon science. I respect doctors, clinical trials and hard evidence. I know some drugs don't work and some carry real risk. But there's a question Washington doesn't ask often enough: who gets to decide how much risk a patient is willing to accept? If I understand the risks, my doctor understands the risks, and there's real evidence a treatment could help, why does a regulator in Washington get the final word on whether I'm allowed to try? Congress already recognized part of this principle when President Trump signed the Right to Try Act into law in 2018. That law was a major step forward because it affirmed something patients facing life-threatening diseases have always known: when approved options are exhausted, and a doctor believes an investigational treatment may help, patients should not be treated as passive observers in their own survival. Right to Try was not the end of that idea. It was the beginning of a patient-centered philosophy that should shape the FDA’s culture more broadly. The same principle should apply when the agency weighs evidence, risk, urgency and access for rare-disease patients. If the patient understands the risk, the physician understands the risk, and there is real evidence that a treatment could help, the system should lean toward partnership instead of paternalism. That’s why Senator Ron Johnson and Representative Diana Harshbarger introduced Right to Try 2.0: to carry that same principle into the next era of medicine, including individualized treatments that do not fit neatly into the FDA’s traditional approval model. They are right to press the issue. But the next leader at the FDA should not have to wait for Congress to force a more patient-centered approach. The FDA already knows that time matters. Its accelerated approval pathway exists precisely because making patients with serious, life-threatening diseases wait years for a traditional clinical endpoint can cost them the thing they can't get back. The agency has used that pathway for multiple DMD treatments already. FIRST-EVER GENE THERAPY FOR HEARING LOSS GETS FDA APPROVAL: 'GROUNDBREAKING' Because waiting is never neutral when you have Duchenne. Every year can mean another loss of strength, another limitation, another piece of independence gone for good. My brother, who also lives with DMD, has seen the other side of this fight, too. Even when a treatment exists, actually getting it can be its own battle. Traveling hours away from home for a multiyear clinical trial sounds manageable in a Washington conference room. It looks very different when you're the one making that trip while your body is working against you as opposed to having access to the therapy at your own hospital. CANCER TREATMENT DELAYS SURGE ACROSS US AS DOCTOR WARNS SYSTEM ‘NEEDS FIXING IMMEDIATELY’ That's why I want the next FDA commissioner to listen to patients like me. We don’t just read about the disease in books or look at it through a microscope — we live with it every day. It’s in us — woven into our DNA. Living with Duchenne has forced me to learn more about drug development and regulatory pathways than I ever expected to know. I want an FDA that works with patients, physicians and rare-disease experts. That's also why I'm going to say something people will have opinions about: I hope whoever leads the FDA brings on Dr. Houman Hemmati as deputy commissioner. He has spent his career in biotech, not politics, building treatments for rare and degenerative diseases instead of just regulating them from the outside. He's also my friend. I know what that sentence invites. Critics will say I'm just trying to get someone I know into the room. They're right that I know him. What they're missing is: he doesn't just know my disease, he's lived it with me. I'm not asking anyone to promise me forever. I'm asking for the chance to fight for the future I still see. I've already outlived what a lot of people expected. I'm not ready to stop. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Senators considering Dr. Overton's nomination have a choice to make too: confirm a commissioner who will treat patients as partners in their own survival, or keep a system that treats us as bystanders to it. It's time. And I'd like Washington to finally understand what mine is worth.

articles.title: Sylvester Stallone Says He Had Bulimia When His Body Became a Dangerous ‘Obsession’
articles.summary: Sylvester Stallone opens up about having the eating disorder bulimia and dealing with anxiety. The “Rocky” and “Rambo” actor is author of a new memoir.
articles.body: Sylvester Stallone is known for playing tough guys and action heroes, but he’s revealing the punishing toll his career took on his mind and body. The actor suffered from an eating disorder, used steroids and endured anxiety attacks, he said in a new interview. At 80, he also reflected on his mental health. “You’re never too old to be in love, never too old to dance with the great memories that you’ve had, and not wallow in the worst swamp of all, which is the swamp of loneliness. That is truly premature burial,” Stallone told The New York Times. The Academy Award-nominated actor has written a new memoir, titled “The Steps.” It takes readers from his childhood — when he slurred his words and “mumbled,” the result of doctors partially paralyzing his face when they used forceps during his delivery — to the highs and lows of fame. Stallone found stardom playing a boxer in “Rocky,” a character he created; then “Rambo,” where he portrayed a troubled Vietnam veteran. Both franchises featured intensely physical roles requiring a body transformation. Here’s what he said about his health journey: He Had Bulimia When he prepared for his role in “Rambo,” Stallone said he wanted to look aggressive, athletic and “more animalistic,” like a jaguar or a cat. “Then it became an obsession. Really bad. It got to the point where I became bulimic,” the actor said. Bulimia is an eating disorder where people binge on food, then make themselves vomit or use laxatives to prevent weight gain. Stallone said he got down to 2.6% body fat when he was in “Rocky III.” That would be considered “dangerously low,” according to the National Academy of Sports Medicine. “I couldn’t hold anything down. Or I didn’t want to keep it down because I became so obsessed with staying at that point of fitness, literally an obsessive body-worship kind of thing,” he recalled. He added that he also periodically took steroids: “You have to. But you do it in a sensitive way — six weeks on, six weeks off… that also took a terrible toll.” He ‘Abused’ His Body Stallone said he once saw his body as his armor, and kept hurting himself by doing his own stunts, calling it “very masochistic.” He’s had nine back operations, two shoulder surgeries and three neck fusions. “I’ve abused my body,” he noted. “Everything is held together with baling wire, but I still want to stay in good shape.” At 80, he called himself “sort of fit,” said he takes a lot of pills to keep going. He Suffered from Anxiety Stallone remembered feeling intense anxiety for the first time when he was 36 and watching early unedited footage from a film. “All of a sudden, I stood up and the hair on my neck went up and I started getting hot and I go, I’m dying, this is it, I’m on my way out,” he recalled. “And then it happened again and again and again. It went away for five years. And then it always seems to happen, like, just as you’re getting ready to go on the Today Show — boom! Anybody got a Xanax? It’s too late. So you’re just sitting there holding onto a chair.” The actor continued to experience anxiety as he got older, feeling the need to leave crowded rooms. It Took Him a Long Time to Understand Love The actor calls his wife of almost 30 years, Jennifer Flavin, “the greatest woman ever.” “I literally didn’t figure out real, true love until I was 70,” Stallone said. “To really have unequivocally true love, that total abandonment, that reckless love that you would jump into a volcano for someone, that came late. And that’s a big pity.”

articles.title: The Healthiest Jams and Which Ones to Avoid, According to Dietitians
articles.summary: Jams are delicious and sweet, but are these fruit spreads healthy? Dietitians share the healthiest types of jams, which to avoid and nutritious jam pairings.
articles.body: Jams, preserves, marmalades — whatever you call these popular fruit-based spreads — you probably have a jar in your pantry or fridge. They’re staple condiments, adding sweetness to toast, sandwiches and savory dishes. Part of what makes jam so delicious is the sugar — and that’s also why it can get a bad rap for being unhealthy. But it’s also made with nutritious fruits packed with vitamins, minerals and fiber. It begs the question: Can jam be healthy? And which types of jam are the most nutritious? We spoke to dietitians to find out. What Is Jam? “At their core, jams are basically a preserved fruit product that is made by boiling the fruit, crushing it, chopping it up, and refining it,” Shannon Stockero, registered dietitian and spokesperson for The Obesity Society, tells TODAY.com. Typically, sugar and an acid are added to the jam along with pectin, a preservative, before it gets jarred. “The (pectin) can provide a thicker consistency, and it’s often used to preserve the fruit so it can be used in its spread form,” says Stockero. Preserves are similar to jams but contain larger chunks of fruit and often seeds, and marmalade is a type of preserve made exclusively from citrus fruits. When it comes to jam vs. jelly, there’s a more notable difference in both the ingredients and nutrition. “Jam and jelly are both made with fruit and sugar, but the main difference is the part of the fruit that’s used,” Natalie Rizzo, dietitian and TODAY.com nutrition editor, tells TODAY.com. “Jam is made with crushed or pureed fruit, so it typically contains some of the fruit’s pulp and has a thicker consistency. Jelly is made from fruit juice, which is strained to remove the pulp and fruit chunks, giving it a smoother consistency,” Rizzo explains. Jelly tends to be more processed than jam, offering less nutritional value. Jam Nutrition The nutrition content of jam will vary based on which type of fruit it contains and how it’s made. Fruits commonly used in jams include strawberries, blackberries, raspberries, peaches, apricots, figs and grapes. A single serving (one tablespoon) of the average fruit jam provides the following, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture database: 55 calories0 grams of protein0 grams of fat15 grams of carbohydrates10 grams of sugar0 grams of fiber Jam is made up almost entirely of carbohydrates, mostly from sugars. “Jam can retain some of the vitamins, minerals and plant compounds found in fruit, but processing and heating can reduce heat-sensitive nutrients like vitamin C,” says Rizzo. Jam generally contains much less fiber than whole fruit, Rizzo says, especially if the skin or seeds have been removed. “I wouldn’t think of jam as a serving of fruit,” Rizzo notes. Can Jam Be Healthy? “Jam can absolutely fit into a healthy diet, but I wouldn’t necessarily call it ‘healthy,’” says Rizzo. Most jams are made from real fruit, such as nutrient-rich berries, but they also have quite a bit of added sugar — around 8 to 12 grams per tablespoon, Rizzo points out. Jam also provides energy in the form of carbohydrates, which can help fuel the body before or after exercise, Stockero notes. The spreads do contain micronutrients that are important for health, says Stockero, but the amount is relatively low compared to whole or mashed fruits. Although the heating process degrades some vitamins, jams will retain minerals and plant compounds. “These include anthocyanins, which are powerful antioxidants found in berries. Those can survive the manufacturing processes,” says Stockero. “Rather than avoiding it completely, think of jam as a condiment that can add sweetness and flavor to nutritious foods.” says Rizzo. The serving size of jam is small, so it can be easy to overdo it and increase your added sugar intake. “The conversation around jams should be more about portion size and the types of foods that you’re having it with,” says Stockero. The American Heart Association recommends adults consume no more than 6–9 teaspoons (25-36 grams) of added sugar per day. Jam can be part of a balanced, nutritious diet, but it’s important to enjoy it in moderation and pair it with whole, nutritious foods which provide additional fiber, protein and healthy fats. “The fiber (especially) can stabilize your blood sugar, which is helpful,” says Stockero. The Healthiest Type of Jam When shopping for jams, dietitians recommend reading the nutrition labels and comparing products. “Approach the jam aisle with curiosity,” says Stockero. The healthiest jams tend to have a few things in common: Fruit is the first ingredientLow or no added sugarMinimal additives “The first thing I look at is the ingredient list,” says Rizzo. Real fruit should be listed as the first ingredient. “These are listed in a way that demonstrates how much each ingredient is within the food, moving from the (highest) amount to the least,” says Stockero. Healthier jams will also contain minimal amounts or no added sugars, the experts note. “I compare the nutrition labels and look for an option with less added sugar,” says Rizzo. The type of sugar also matters. Ideally, the jam should be sweetened with fruit or fruit juice instead of refined sugars. “Jams with ‘no sugar added’ or reduced-sugar varieties can be good options, but check what they’re sweetened with because those terms don’t automatically mean the product is healthier,” says Rizzo. The ingredient list should also be relatively short, simple and easy to pronounce, according to Rizzo. Look for jams with fewer additives, such as preservatives and stabilizers. Ultimately, the healthiest jam is probably homemade, the experts note. This allows you to control the fruit content, added sugars and other ingredients. “A great option is a chia jam made with mashed berries and chia seeds. It gives you the fruit plus additional fiber and healthy fats from the chia seeds, and you can control how much sweetener goes into it,” says Rizzo. Sugar-free jams may be a healthier option for people who need to limit their sugar intake, such as people with diabetes, says Stockero. But always talk to your doctor if you have questions. Jams To Limit or Avoid The least healthy jams tend to contain added sugar or high-fructose corn syrup as the first ingredient. “Looking at the label, seeing that would be my biggest concern, and something we maybe want to stray away from,” says Stockero. These refined sugar-laden jams tend to contain a relatively small amount of real fruit, says Rizzo — many commercial jams offer just 35% or less fruit per serving. Is It Healthy to Eat Jam Every Day? “A small amount of jam each day can fit into a balanced diet. But you have to be mindful of the serving size — stick to one tablespoon or less,” says Rizzo. The experts emphasize that the healthiest way to enjoy jam in your regular diet is by pairing it with whole foods rich in macro- and micronutrients. “A little bit of jam can make a nutritious food more enjoyable, and that can actually help you stick with healthy eating habits long term,” says Rizzo. Most Nutritious Pairings for Jam “Pair jam with foods that provide protein, fiber or healthy fats,” says Rizzo. That makes the jam part of a more filling, nutrient-rich meal or snack rather than just a source of added sugar. Some of the healthiest pairings for jam include: Whole grain toastGreek yogurtNut butterSeeded crackersOatmealCottage cheeseChia pudding

articles.title: Cheese Recalled Nationwide Amid E. Coli Outbreak
articles.summary: Cheese made with raw milk is being recalled nationwide after public health officials linked it to an E. coli outbreak that’s sickened people in nine states.
articles.body: Cheese made with raw milk is being recalled across the country after public health officials linked it to an ongoing E. coli outbreak. Sierra Nevada Cheese Company initiated a voluntary recall of all of the company’s Graziers Raw Milk Cheese, which includes medium cheddar, sharp cheddar, jalapeño jack and Monterey jack cheeses, according to the Food and Drug Administration. The recall came amid a public health investigation into an E. coli outbreak that has sickened at least 13 people across nine states, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention explain. That includes eight people who were hospitalized and three more who were hospitalized due to hemolytic uremic syndrome, a potentially life-threatening complication from an E. coli infection. “Sierra Nevada Cheese Company is voluntarily recalling all Graziers Raw Milk Cheese currently on the market,” the company said in a statement on Facebook. “This action is being taken due to reported illnesses associated with Graziers Raw Milk Medium Cheddar. At this time, the investigation has not been narrowed down to a specific lot or date code,” the statement continues. “Out of an abundance of caution, we are expanding the recall to include all Graziers Raw Milk Cheese.” Here’s what to know about the recalled raw milk cheese and the E. coli outbreak. Which Cheeses Are Recalled? The recall, initiated on Sept. 25, 2026, affects all Sierra Nevada Graziers raw milk cheese on the market right now. That includes four types of the brand’s cheese: Graziers Raw Milk Medium Cheddar, 16 oz, UPC: 6-87652-16501-3Graziers Raw Milk Medium Cheddar, 12/8 oz, UPC: 6-87652-16506-8Graziers Raw Milk Sharp Cheddar, 12/8 oz, UPC: 6-87652-16507-5Graziers Raw Milk Jalapeño Jack, 12/8 oz, UPC: 6-87652-16403-0Graziers Raw Milk Monterey Jack, 12/8 oz, UPC: 6-87652-16400-9 The recall also affects 5-lb loaves sold to wholesalers and food service customers: 6425: Graziers Raw Milk Monterey Jack, 2/5 lb6426: Graziers Raw Milk Jalapeño Jack, 2/5 lb6510: Graziers Raw Milk Medium Cheddar, 2/5lb6511: Graziers Raw Milk Sharp Cheddar, 2/5 lb Where Was the Recalled Cheese Sold? The recalled cheese was sold at retailers nationwide and online, the FDA says, but the agency does not mention specific stores. Recalled Graziers raw milk cheese was also available to wholesalers and food service customers. Why Is the Cheese Being Recalled? The raw milk cheese from Sierra Nevada Graziers has been recalled after public health officials linked it to an ongoing E. coli outbreak. Illnesses related to the outbreak began between July 7, 2026, and Aug. 26, 2026, the CDC explains. As of Sept. 25, 2026, the CDC has counted 13 illnesses, eight of which hospitalized people. Of those sickened in the outbreak, more than half are age 5 or younger. Cases have been detected in nine states, with most cases in California and Nevada. Officials interviewed nine people in the outbreak, and all of them reported eating the raw milk cheese before getting sick. Raw milk is milk that has not been through the pasteurization process that kills bacteria. Raw milk and raw milk dairy products have been linked to numerous foodborne illness outbreaks in the past. The actual number of people sickened in the outbreak is likely higher than this, the CDC notes, because many people recover without medical attention. And it can take three to four weeks to determine if a sick person is truly associated with a larger outbreak like this. E. Coli Infection Symptoms Symptoms of an E. coli infection typically begin within three to four days after eating tainted food, the Mayo Clinic says, but may take up to nine days, the FDA notes. The most common symptoms of an E. coli infection include: Loose stools, which may be mild or serious, and watery or bloodyStomach cramps, tenderness or painUpset stomach and vomiting Low fever For otherwise healthy people, an E. coli infection is unpleasant but not serious and does not require special medical treatment. However, sometimes E. coli infections can cause severe symptoms or complications, including serious dehydration that requires hospitalization to treat. An E. coli infection may also lead to hemolytic uremic syndrome, which is a type of life-threatening kidney failure. Young children and older adults are more likely to get E. coli infections, the Mayo Clinic says, and they’re more likely to have severe complications if they do get sick. In the current outbreak, more than half of the cases are in kids age 5 or younger, and three people have been hospitalized with hemolytic uremic syndrome. What to Do if You Purchased Recalled Cheese If you purchased any of the recalled raw milk cheese, you should not eat it, the FDA urges. Because the cheese has a long shelf life, it’s important to check your fridge for any recalled product that may be there. “Consumers should not consume any Graziers Raw Milk Cheese currently in their refrigerator and should dispose of the product,” the company said in the statement. “We are incredibly grateful for the trust and support of our customers and community,” the statement continues, “and we appreciate your understanding as we take this precautionary step.”

articles.title: Somali army clashes with local forces for control of Baidoa
articles.summary: The latest outbreak of fighting in the South West State city stranded civilians unable to flee or reach hospitals.
articles.body:
Intense clashes have broken out in the Somali city of Baidoa between government forces and fighters loyal to the ousted regional president.

Fighter jets and drones were reported as the hostilities flared on Monday in the South West State city after thousands of local fighters entered the city in the morning. Violence has plagued the city in recent weeks as the army seeks to maintain the control it wrested earlier this year.

“The national army confronted them, inflicted heavy casualties and drove them out of the city,” senior army commander Mohamed Ali said, according to the AFP news agency. He added that the local fighters had vehicles loaded with explosives and explosive drones.

A number of states in Somalia oppose President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. His government sent troops to oust the head of South West State, Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen in March. Laftagareen has repeatedly attempted to retake the area, including the administrative capital of Baidoa.

In a statement , Laftagareen congratulated fighters for the operation, saying that the aim was to “maintain security [and] restore stability and diversity” in Baidoa.

The medical NGO Doctors Without Borders, known by its French acronym MSF, said three people had died including a healthcare worker.

“There were heavy clashes all day in the city,” local resident Hussein Abdifatah told AFP. “Most of the civilians have difficulties fleeing because both sides are fighting everywhere.”

Medical teams working with the Ministry of Health at Baidoa’s Bay Regional Hospital said they had received 69 patients affected by the violence, including five children.

Roads leading to hospitals in Baidoa were blocked, and MSF said it is concerned that many wounded people are unable to access treatment.

“This is the third time in six weeks that fighting has erupted in Baidoa, with devastating consequences for civilians,” Dr Elshafie Mohammed, MSF’s Somalia representative, said. “It is unacceptable that civilians and healthcare are being caught up in violence.”

A health facility was also reportedly severely damaged and an ambulance looted, the aid agency said. Two medical staff working with its teams were robbed and one was injured.

Fighting erupted in Baidoa on August 17, when Bay Regional Hospital reported four deaths and 94 people wounded, and again on September 3 , when 71 people were treated for injuries and one death was recorded.

articles.title: Sylvester Stallone reveals surprising health struggle behind his famously ripped physique
articles.summary: Sylvester Stallone revealed he became bulimic while prepping for "Rambo" and reached 2.6% body fat during "Rocky III" in a stunning new interview.
articles.body: Sylvester Stallone is sharing some health obstacles he has faced while playing physically demanding roles over the decades. The Academy Award-nominated actor, 80, revealed during an interview with The New York Times that he has suffered from an eating disorder. While prepping for his role in the 1982 movie "Rambo," Stallone — who has authored a new memoir, titled "The Steps" — said he took pains to appear more "animalistic," drawing inspiration from jaguars and cats. MEN FACE NEW PRESSURE TO STAY ‘HOT’ AS THEY AGE — AND IT’S NOT JUST ABOUT LIVING LONGER "Then it became an obsession. Really bad. It got to the point where I became bulimic," he said during the interview. Bulimia nervosa is an eating disorder marked by episodes of binge eating — consuming a large amount of food while feeling a loss of control — followed by purging behaviors such as vomiting, excessive use of laxatives or diuretics, fasting or excessive exercise, according to the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH). "I couldn’t hold anything down. Or I didn’t want to keep it down because I became so obsessed with staying at that point of fitness, literally an obsessive body-worship kind of thing," Stallone shared. CONTROVERSIAL STREAMER CLAVICULAR EXPLAINS VIRAL 'LOOKSMAXXING' TREND AS GEN Z ADOPTS EXTREME REGIMEN The actor said that while filming "Rocky III," he reached his lowest body fat of 2.6%. The National Academy of Sports Medicine classifies body fat as "dangerously low" if it falls below 8% for men ages 20–69 and below 14% for women ages 20–69. Stallone also admitted that he took steroids during some time periods. "You have to," he said. "But you do it in a sensitive way — six weeks on, six weeks off … that also took a terrible toll." Years of injuries sustained while doing his own stunts — something he described as "very masochistic" — have also taken a toll on Stallone’s body, he said, leading to multiple surgeries on his back, shoulder and neck. Stallone also revealed that he has dealt with anxiety over the decades, recounting the first incident while watching footage from one of his films when he was 36 years old. "All of a sudden, I stood up and the hair on my neck went up and I started getting hot and I go, ‘I’m dying, this is it, I’m on my way out,’" he said in the interview. The actor said the panic attacks happened "again and again and again," often resurfacing before high-profile television appearances. As he aged, Stallone continued to experience anxiety and sometimes felt compelled to leave crowded rooms. "There are so many examples of what can take place in Sylvester Stallone's life that have led him to moments of objectivity and body awareness," Pollack, who has not treated Stallone, told Fox News Digital. The expert suggested that a desire to maintain his success may have fueled Stallone’s rigid routines, steroid use, intense performance expectations, fear of failure, and the pressures associated with the entertainment industry. "The idea that a man enhances his appearance to remain consistent with his own public image and internal comfort goes back decades — [Stallone] isn’t the first, and he isn’t the last," Pollack said. "And through his career, one could surmise the need to be able to put all of that together and keep it consistent as he goes through the development and life cycles of maturation, not only in his brain, but also in his body." "Eating disorders continue to be misconstrued as primarily female illnesses," she told Fox News Digital.

articles.summary: HOPE CME 2026 in Lucknow highlighted personalized infertility care beyond IVF, featuring AI and robotic surgery, organized by Ajanta Hospital’s Dr Gita Khanna.

articles.title: 31 get prosthetic limbs, mobility aids at Ayodhya outreach camp
articles.summary: Ayodhya outreach camp by Ashok Singhal Foundation provides free prosthetic limbs and mobility aids to 31 people, Sept 27-Oct 1 at Karsevakpuram.
articles.body: Lucknow: Reaching out to individuals who have lost limbs in accidents, the Ashok Singhal Foundation distributed prosthetic limbs and mobility aid to 31 people during a special outreach programme in Ayodhya.Organised as part of the centenary birth celebrations of former international president of Vishwa Hindu Parishad late Ashok Singhal, the five-day camp is being held at Karsevakpuram from Sept 27 to Oct 1.The initiative seeks to identify and support people requiring rehabilitation and assistive devices, helping them regain mobility and independence.Now in its sixth edition, the annual programme invites specially-abled people to register in advance, following which health workers and technical experts assess their requirements.Beneficiaries are provided artificial limbs, calipers, crutches, hearing aids, spectacles and other assistive devices free of cost.“Registered beneficiaries are called in advance so that health workers can take precise measurements before ordering prosthetic fitments. Similarly, eye examinations are carried out beforehand to ensure suitable corrective lenses are provided,” said Amardeep Kamal of Ashok Singhal Eye Care Hospital.Ayodhya mayor Girish Pati Tripathi said such programmes help restore confidence and dignity among differently-abled people while enabling them to lead more independent lives.Among the beneficiaries were Shakuntala and her daughter Surekha from Rae Bareli, who lost their legs after being hit by a truck three years ago.Another beneficiary, Mamta from Etawah, lost a leg in a railway accident at Hazrat Nizamuddin station while travelling for a Delhi police recruitment examination.Treasurer of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Mahesh Bhagchandka is the chairperson of the foundation while former general secretary of the Tust Champat Rai is among the founding members of the organisation.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Pune city at high risk of Zika cases in future, states NIV research
articles.summary: NIV study warns Pune may face more Zika cases due to high Aedes aegypti density and transmission-linked mutations; 2024 outbreak had 109 cases, no fetal defects found.
articles.body: Pune: High Aedes aegypti density and transmission-enhancing mutations in circulating Zika virus strains have left the city with a possibility of an increase in cases in future, a National Institute of Virology (NIV) study of Pune’s 2024 monsoon outbreak has warned.The study, recently published in Indian Journal of Medical Research, found that 26.5% of Aedes aegypti mosquito pools collected from neighbourhoods reporting cases tested positive for Zika RNA. The researchers cautioned that the positivity rate was limited to outbreak-affected neighbourhoods and did not represent the general mosquito population of the city.“These collections were done in the neighbourhood of positive cases and so the high positivity is limited to the neighbourhood and is not the virus positivity in the general mosquito population,” said Kavita Lole, one of the authors associated with the study.“Regarding the E-V437M mutation, it has been established that this mutation helps the virus in efficiently spreading itself. Fortunately, we have not detected any mutations similar to those reported from Brazil that are known to cause microcephaly in the newborns,” she said.Genomic analysis showed that the virus strains belonged to the Asian lineage and carried mutations that could favour transmission. The study said the E-V473M mutation, found in the majority of current Zika virus strains in India, may have contributed to greater peripheral viraemia, efficient mosquito infection and viral spread.Greater peripheral viraemia refers to a higher concentration of viral particles circulating in the peripheral bloodstream. It generally indicates active viral replication or the spread of the virus beyond its initial site of infection. However, mutations associated with severe fetal outcomes, including microcephaly reported during the 2015–17 Zika outbreak in the Americas, were not detected in the Pune strains.The study was conducted between June and Sept 2024, when the city recorded 109 confirmed Zika cases. Forty-five of them were pregnant women. Adult mosquitoes and larvae were collected from the houses of reported cases and surrounding premises within a 400m radius.After the outbreak, Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) followed up with pregnant women who had contracted Zika. PMC’s assistant health officer Rajesh Dighe said fetal growth remained normal among those monitored.He said, “In 2024, there was an outbreak of Zika virus limited to certain pockets in Erandwane, Mundhwa, Pashan, Warje and Yerawada. We had reported 109 cases, of which a significant number of patients were pregnant women.”Dighe said, “We had followed up with all these women even after the outbreak subsided to ensure that none of the fetuses were affected. Fortunately, all the fetuses reported normal growth and did not report any Zika-related congenital deformities. PMC had not reported a single Zika case in the city since the 2024 outbreak.”Though Zika infection is generally mild in adults, it can cause serious neurological and developmental complications in fetuses, particularly when contracted during pregnancy.
